Test-only: the repeated rows are `git` argument vectors and arms of a shell `gh` stub that model GitHub protocol responses. They are fixture data for one forged-comment scenario, not production dispatch logic.

Each branch validates a different typed model (initiative, definition, workspace, plan, graph) whose validate() has its own signature and error shape; there is no common row type to tabulate, and the graph arm maps violations rather than extending directly.

Test-only fixture builder: the repeated rows are fake GitHub CLI responses keyed by command, the same shape already allowlisted for autonomous_integration_base_sync.rs. Attribution moved to this function when #3472 fixed function_ranges_brace().

CLI integration test: the repeated rows are JSON-field assertions over one timeline response fixture. Assertion data, not production branching. Attribution moved to this function when #3472 fixed function_ranges_brace().

The arms match distinct EditAction variants with different bindings and different guard policies; the inner ifs each raise a differently named violation with its own message. A table would have to carry a closure per row and would hide which policy produced which violation id.

The genuinely uniform part — the four signal penalties — is already a table with a single dispatcher loop. The remaining branches each apply a different scoring formula (flat credit, clamped coverage ratio, cache-hit rate, churn ratio) to a different field, so they share no row shape.

The branches are cumulative escalation thresholds, not parallel cases: each adds a different role set to the same accumulator, one arm removes a role, and one returns early. Order is semantic, so a predicate table would change behaviour.
